source.title: Automated Interpretability and Feature Discovery in Language Models with Agents

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies a multi-metric explanation procedure to SAE features and explicitly reports one as polysemantic and another as monosemantic. This is a conceptual test of feature ambiguity, but it does not test any listed version as stated: the reported case studies are SAE features, not estimates of polysemanticity among neurons or tests of the listed mechanisms and measurement dependencies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE-feature case studies with explicit polysemantic/monosemantic classifications; these are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version because the versions concern neurons, prevalence, causes, architecture comparisons, shared-feature reinterpretations, or dependence on measurement choices. Raw-neuron results concern finding category markers and validating their explanations, not measuring how often neurons respond to unrelated inputs. Other reported numbers about ranking methods, costs, and clustering do not measure the claim.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper for an automated interpretability agent. Polysemanticity detection is a built-in step of its own explanation pipeline. The two polysemantic/monosemantic classifications are single SAE-feature demonstrations of that method, not neuron-level measurements. The raw MLP-neuron experiment in a weight-sparse transformer reports marker discovery and validation accuracy, not how often neurons respond to unrelated inputs. The paper reports only its own method's performance, so it is T4, not T2 as the reader proposed.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that agentic iterative multi-metric hypothesis testing yields sharper, more falsifiable explanations than one-shot autointerp (refined hypotheses win 64-83% of features). They conclude that it discovers language-specific and safety-relevant features, including a causal refusal-steering demonstration, and that it transfers to raw MLP neurons in weight-sparse transformers (about 75% validation accuracy). Polysemanticity detection is presented as a feature of the method, not as a finding about prevalence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an agentic hypothesis-refinement and statistical-discovery pipeline on language-model SAE features and raw MLP activations; it does not reproduce the original vision-neuron analysis or its method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that explanation quality varies with the hypothesis-generating LLM, and that clustering results vary with FeatureFinder hyperparameters. It does not show that the polysemantic classification changes with activation range or scoring choice.

fits_no_version.finding: The multi-metric refinement pipeline classifies SAE feature L0 F9004 as monosemantic (French informal phrasing). It flags SAE feature L4 F12773 as polysemantic because code/equations and medical/scientific-term hypotheses remain comparably ranked.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some language-model SAE features converge on one explanation under iterative multi-metric testing, while others retain competing explanations.

fits_no_version.finding: In a weight-sparse GPT-2-style code model, marker MLP neurons for 16 Python syntax categories show very large effect sizes (e.g., d=73.9, 152.3). The authors attribute this to the 'monosemantic nature of neurons in weight-sparse models', but no polysemanticity rate is measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons in weight-sparse transformers include highly selective markers for syntactic categories (bears loosely on V5, but only selected neurons, no prevalence).

record.problems: The polysemanticity case study is a single SAE feature and does not estimate prevalence; the paper does not establish that the competing explanations correspond to unrelated inputs. The raw-neuron experiment uses one weight-sparse model and reports marker-discovery validation rather than a neuron-polysemanticity rate. The paper is under review.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted. The raw MLP-neuron discovery and test-accuracy results concern category-marker discovery and explanation validation, not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: No share of transformer MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens, and no per-layer comparison. Raw neurons are studied only in one weight-sparse model, for marker discovery.
No test of superposition as a cause.
No test of initialization, regularization or noise as a cause.
No controlled comparison of polysemanticity share across architectures or training. The weight-sparse neurons are only asserted to be monosemantic.
No reanalysis of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No comparison of polysemanticity classification across activation ranges or scoring schemes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests' and tranche T2 are wrong: the paper never measures how often neurons or features are polysemantic. It names no rate behind its remark that baseline-winning features are 'typically' poorly defined or polysemantic. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Vision classifiers and image-neuron responses, including InceptionV1.
No estimate of the share of transformer MLP neurons that respond to unrelated tokens or contexts, or comparison of that share across layers.
No test of superposition or whether feature count exceeds neuron count as a cause of polysemanticity.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise causing polysemanticity when capacity is sufficient.
No controlled comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization for polysemanticity share, or associated performance cost.
No test of whether canonical neuron mixtures share a feature or whether genuinely unrelated mixtures are rare.
No comparison of classifications across activation-range choices or explanation-scoring procedures.

rows.subject: SAE feature L0 F9004
rows.operation_detail: The authors' refinement pipeline evaluated competing feature explanations with a seven-metric battery and classified the feature as monosemantic.

conditions.value: Gemma-2 family; specific model not stated for this case

rows.measure: Feature-level polysemanticity classification and ranked explanations
rows.value: The feature was classified as monosemantic; top-ranked refined explanations identified informal French phrasing and colloquial syntax, particularly in technology/troubleshooting contexts.
rows.note: This is an SAE feature case study, not a neuron-level prevalence estimate. The table reports separate hypothesis metrics and rankings; the stated monosemantic classification is the outcome recorded here.
rows.check: Subject is an SAE feature (Gemma-2 SAE, layer 0), not a neuron. The monosemantic label is the output of the study's own pipeline, shown as a method demonstration. It cannot bear on any neuron-level version. State 'observed' has no version to be checked against.

rows.subject: SAE feature L4 F12773
rows.operation_detail: The authors' refinement pipeline evaluated competing feature explanations with a seven-metric battery and flagged the feature as polysemantic.

conditions.value: Gemma-2 family; specific model not stated for this case

rows.measure: Feature-level polysemanticity classification and ranked explanations
rows.value: The feature was flagged as polysemantic because semantically distinct hypotheses remained competitive; examples included coding snippets/equations and technical-scientific discourse.
rows.note: This records the study's explicit classification and examples of competing explanations. It does not establish that the interpretations correspond to unrelated inputs or test whether the classification changes with measurement choices.
rows.check: Subject is an SAE feature, not a neuron. The polysemantic flag is the study's own method output on one hand-picked case. The two competing hypotheses are 'coding snippets and equations' vs 'medical research' terms, and are not shown to be unrelated inputs. It is a demonstration of the method, not a measurement of the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
